scope: Preparation map for one cumulative RAFT export after primary adjudication. No export, transcript, corpus, updater, training, or accepted-artifact mutation.

rules_to_implement: Only attributed letter prose enters question/answer/grounding; headings, addresses, datelines, summaries, notes, footnotes, bibliography and navigation stay in audit metadata.
Keep composition, posting, receipt, reading and demonstrated-knowledge dates distinct; incoming availability is a conservative bound and never replaces the Darwin response date.
Use one established Darwin response or safely dated response section per transcript; preserve scoped relationships and deduplicate shared response bodies.
Unresolved transcription artifacts, dates, attribution, text scope or source identity hold an entry explicitly; never synthesize a prompt.

paths.role: accepted legacy direct/knowledge graph and relation definitions
source identity, XML constraints, body eligibility and provenance
composed accepted graph, nodes, scoped sections, receipt events and candidates
additive remaining review ledgers; include only parent-adjudicated files

example_keys.knowledge: cross-correspondent observations / incoming_knowledge_dates with source evidence

paths.role: authoritative v2 parent-adjudicated ledgers; select status=parent_adjudicated
integrity verification and input hashes, not adjudication

example_keys.grounding: letter_adjudications[].{letter_id,disposition,voice,training_export_ready,paragraphs_read,source}; use only Darwin individual voice and eligible scope

paths.role: scoped corrections/additions; apply after base group

direct_pairs.source: direct_reply_pairs plus accepted graph edges whose relationship is replies_to/replies_to equivalent
direct_pairs.direction: incoming_id is question; outgoing_id must be Darwin-authored response
required: training_export_ready explicitly true only after final checks
direct_pairs.body_dedup: one response letter may produce multiple scoped links but shared Darwin prose must be emitted once per selected transcript unit

precedence: never infer from whole body when a scope exists
hold_if: scope is absent for a multi-topic response

knowledge_dates.source: cross_correspondent_knowledge, receipt_events, dated_sections, legacy receipt evidence
knowledge_dates.semantics: known_by_date is an upper bound on Darwin knowledge, not delivery or composition
knowledge_dates.ordering: incoming must be strictly earlier than response date when used for retrieval; same-day cases require explicit ordering evidence

include: accepted date policy and body scope
not consumed as an answer in a selected pair unless scoped remainder is explicitly retained

supplemental_recovered_sources.route: candidate followup reports and source manifests -> primary adjudication -> additive ledger only if accepted
supplemental_recovered_sources.rule: never read candidate files as authoritative graph edges; preserve source URL/hash/time and keep third-party prose out of Darwin grounding

precedence_and_dedup: Primary-adjudicated ledgers override Luna/reviewer proposals; accepted graphs are authoritative only for the period whose builder composes them.
Within a period, base ledger precedes explicitly named additive correction/addendum; identical relationship keys are retained once, with the latest explicit scoped correction recorded in audit.
A retained prior relationship is carried forward once and does not become a new pair merely because another period/context ledger repeats it.
Deduplicate by stable letter IDs plus relationship and response scope, never by nearest date, subject, URL alone, or text similarity.
Preserve original CSV/XML dates and hashes; inferred known-by/receipt dates are separate fields and cannot rewrite source metadata.

reusable_entrypoints.use: v2 period ledger validation/composition; do not invoke during export preparation
1837-1843 graph composition and scoped text checks
maps remaining 1837-1843 inputs; not an exporter

schema_mismatches_primary_must_settle: 1828-1836 uses legacy graph/receipt structures and lacks the v2 ledger envelope; define a normalized adapter and retain legacy relation semantics.
1837-1843 graph edges use source/target/type while v2 ledgers use incoming_id/outgoing_id and relationship; define direction conversion, especially reverse correspondent replies.
Graph nodes, v2 letter_adjudications, and Beagle dispositions use different voice/text-scope field names; define one export eligibility and remainder-scope vocabulary.
Some accepted relationships are section-dependent or dated-section scoped, while RAFT transcript schema has one transcript-level date; settle transcript splitting/date representation before export.
Beagle additive ledgers expose retained_prior_relationships and addenda outside the period batch sequence; define ordering and duplicate precedence explicitly.

Source provenance varies between body_source/metadata_provenance, embedded graph source objects, and legacy audit paths; require one audit-sidecar schema with source URL, retrieval time, bytes, SHA-256 and pin.
training_export_ready is intentionally false in current ledgers; primary must define the final transition gate and ensure no candidate/review record is mistaken for approval.
Legacy unlocated/reference nodes attest events or receipt without text; decide whether they remain audit-only (recommended by policy) and prevent prompt generation.
